$comment: The AGREED SET of published Fluxtion authoring resources a generated project references.
spec-authoring-experience.md D-AX1c: a project POINTS at these; it never restates them, because one
edit upstream should improve every reader rather than being re-delivered per project.
STATUS IS NOT DECORATION. 'proposed' entries are this session's recommendation and await the owner's
sign-off; 'excluded' entries are deliberate and carry the reason. Bundles must reference only
'agreed' entries — shipping a 'proposed' one would make the sign-off meaningless.
Structure is checked by ReferenceSetTest (offline, in CI). Reachability is checked by
tools/bench/reference-set-bench.py, deliberately NOT in mvn test: mkdocs --strict cannot see external
URLs and SpecLinksResolveTest only walks docs/specs, so this is the only thing that checks them — but
a network fetch in the unit suite would make the build flake on someone else's outage.

resources.why: How to author Fluxtion with an LLM, and the compile/run loop the rest of the stack serves.
The author orientation, including the source-gen triage table that maps a build error to its fix.
The blessed shape and its gotchas; carries the worked auditLog chaining example.
The FluxtionSpringConfig field table: nodeBeans, ignoredBeans, eventTypes and the XML shape.

resources.note: Overlaps the orientation heavily. Round 05 found two sessions reporting it added nothing they used. Include only if the owner wants the canon cited directly.

resources.note: EXCLUDED until telaminai/fluxtion#22 is resolved. It states audit 'falls out of how the processor is generated' — true for which nodes fired, false for what each node reports — so an author concludes no instrumentation is needed.
